newsitem.title: USA: Cold wave to follow snow, rain in central U.S..
newsitem.headline: Cold wave to follow snow, rain in central U.S..

text.p: Frigid weather, rain and snow hit the central U.S. over the weekend and more cold, which has the potential to hurt winter wheat, was forecast Wednesday and Thursday from North Dakota to northern Texas and east to Ohio, meteorologists said.

"We are watching it, because if it gets any colder it could put some winter wheat in danger," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, referring to a mid-week cold spell that may produce lows in the teens and 20s degrees Fahrenheit, from Kansas to Texas.
Lows early Monday dropped to 14 degrees in Goodland, Kan., and to 26 degrees Sunday morning in Amarillo, Texas.
"It was very cold, but probably not quite cold enough to damage the crop," said Burgio of the hard red winter wheat.
A weekend storm dumped one to two feet of snow in the western Dakotas and rain and snow in the eastern Dakotas, all of which will delay fieldwork and probably increase spring flooding.
Farmers in the flooded Red River Valley, "are not going to be in the fields for weeks," said Burgio.
